title: The Narrow Edge: Full Hands
summary: Ring out one opposing piece. Each turn gives both pieces baseline movement and a five-card tactical hand.
designQuestion: Can full-hand sequencing create threats, costly defenses, and counter-pressure on only 19 hexes?
result: Ochre wins on turn five with a four-card line after Indigo twice prevents a live ring-out.
findings: Full hands create setup, payoff, and counterplay within one turn.
Brace matters because each use cancels a live edge push.
Relay turns an edge rescue into a counterattack instead of resetting play.
The finishing hand needs four effects in the correct order.

config.movementRule: Move each piece once. Interleave those moves with any cards in the five-card hand.

rules: Each piece can move to one adjacent empty hex each turn.
Play each card in the shown hand at most once.
Interleave baseline moves and card plays in any order.
A push moves its target one hex directly away from its source.
Brace cancels the next push against its piece, then clears.
Drive requires Off-Balance and can follow into the target's old hex.

cardLibrary.Off-Balance: Mark an adjacent enemy. Drive can push it.
cardLibrary.Drive: Push an adjacent Off-Balance enemy. You may follow into its old hex.
cardLibrary.Shove: Push an adjacent enemy one hex.
cardLibrary.Pin: The target cannot use its next baseline move.
cardLibrary.Dash: Move one friendly piece to an adjacent empty hex.
cardLibrary.Relay: Swap two friendly pieces within two hexes.
cardLibrary.Sidestep: Move one friendly piece to an adjacent empty hex.
cardLibrary.Countershove: Push an adjacent enemy one hex.
cardLibrary.Brace: Cancel the next push against one friendly piece.
cardLibrary.Cleanse: Remove Pin and Off-Balance from one friendly piece.
